title: From S_2E to E^NP: near-maximum circuit lower bounds
credit: Korten (FOCS 2021); Chen, Hirahara, Ren (STOC 2024), arXiv:2309.12912; Li (STOC 2024), arXiv:2310.17762.
premise_risks: ECCC TR26-118 (Ren–Williams, Jul 2026, unrefereed): status claim that E^{prMA}/1 requires 2^n/n circuits; only affects the 'state of the art' summary, not the statement.
arXiv:2605.03306 (Hitchcock, May 2026 preprint): comeagerness result in S₂E; context only.
plain: Prove E^NP is not contained in SIZE[2^n/n] (or even SIZE[2^{epsilon n}] for some eps>0 infinitely often); equivalently, put Range Avoidance in FP^NP for the relevant circuit classes, improving Li's FS_2^P algorithm.
math: Prove that for some ε > 0 there is L ∈ E^NP such that for infinitely many n, L ∩ {0,1}^n has no circuit of size 2^{εn} (stronger: for all large n). Related target (not claimed equivalent at this size): AVOID ∈ FP^NP, which by Korten (2021) implies E^NP ⊄ SIZE[2^n/n].
review_note: Context (AI-lab announcement, treated as correct): OpenAI 378, The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False. Claims superlinear circuit lower bounds for a language in E^NP on infinitely many lengths, which is new for E^NP. Superlinear is far below the board's 2^{eps n} target, so this does not resolve it, but it changes the stated best-known E^NP lower bound.
